![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/189bc3083101fa113811891be78d57b626acca68856318304266a1d16fc9e251.png)

The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/5344a6c4972c03c9177419daa2f74be81ecabfad1db5c10f8dcbce794b07b265.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $(-\frac{\pi }{2},0],$ we get the quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},0].
$$
